column9: EXAMINED, NOT UNEXAMINED, and the distinction is the point. proxy_attribution.csv prices three proxy changes at up to 2.3 Mt each on a 223 Mt module, and it is tempting to read them as a bracket. They are not one: all three are CORRECTIONS ALREADY APPLIED, and the readings they replaced are known worse rather than co-defensible - applied manure rode livestock_total, which ignores that manure goes to fields, and rice synthetic nitrogen rode undifferentiated fertilizer_N. A bracket between the current reading and a superseded one would make the bound look rigorous while resting on a proxy nobody defends. The module therefore stays declared-unpriced for placement, and closing it needs a second reading that is defensible TODAY - a district crop or livestock record independent of the census panel

column9: rc62: THE ONE WITHIN-PROVINCE TEST OCAC MAKES POSSIBLE, and built-up fails it. OCAC prints KARACHI as a named sub-area of SINDH, so for exactly one district-group the publication states what share of a province's industrial furnace oil it takes: 90.4, 90.9, 90.9 and 82.0 percent across FY2021-22 to FY2024-25. The cube's built-up raster gives the same eight-district Karachi shape 47.9 percent of Sindh - low by very nearly a factor of two. Built-up REMAINS the executed within-province surface, because no held evidence places industrial furnace oil below the province anywhere else in the country and a surface that is wrong in Karachi is not thereby right somewhere else. What changes is that it stops being a bare point estimate: this row prices the one place it can be checked, and Lahore's 12.2 percent of Punjab - which rests on the same raster and has no fuel evidence behind it at all - inherits that demonstrated error as a bracket rather than a silence. The acquisition that would collapse it is an industrial fuel panel below the province: REQ-CMI-01, drafted and unsent.
